title: What's your workflow for 3D animation? How do you reach 80% or 90% or 95% with AI and what do you do to reach 100%? Tools, pipelines, directions, workflows, discussions are welcome!
author: wimblecraft
selftext: This topic evolves with model releases and capability improvements, your latest understanding works best for this discussion.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: :( I found a wonderful 3D modeler and animator to join my project. He does work in an hour that I couldn’t do in a week, even with AI

replies.author: wimblecraft
replies.body:
What does he do that you don't? 

The path to mastery is meaningful and learning from a master is the best way to go about it!

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Why would I learn from a master, when I can instead have a master on my team and we can work together?

replies.author: wimblecraft
replies.body: Please share insights if you do, this is a discussion thread after all. It's alright if you don't.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
My insight is that having a teammate unlocks just a ton of new possibilities for game development. It lets everyone on the team specialize—I can specialize in music and programming, he can specialize in artwork and 3D modeling, someone else can specialize in writing, another person specializes in level design. 

Because he spends 100% of his focus on artwork, he’s damn good at it.

replies.author: wimblecraft
replies.body: Thank you. That makes total sense.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
80% isn't that expecting too much, I get about 40%-50% at best. 

Step1 is making an detailed reference. Step2 is to use the reference with every local and online AI I have access to. Step3 is taking the best aspects of every model and merging them. Step4 is Auto retopo. Step5 is UV mapping. Step6 is baking.

Step7 for Skinned meshes I will rig using auto rig tools.

comments.author: piXelicidio
comments.body:
It sounds like the final objective/motivation is to reach 100% AI-animation even if it cost more and have to spend more time switching between services, pipelines, workflows.... than doing it yourself, buying it from stock or hiring an animator to help.

So to answer your question, to reach 100%, you just wait for the ai-model/online service that can do it.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: I don't use ai for that. Instant 100%

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
lol @ 80%. Hell, I basically do 100% myself. I'll use AI for animation references via video gen if I don't have an exact idea of how the anatomy would move but it's really not worth the effort of having it actually try to animate. I have given it reference poses though.. which kind of leads into my custom workflow. I had AI build me tools to basically optimize my workflow with animation. It's in engine, with immediate feedback to see animations on actual characters real time, able to swap and compare shapes, etc. I can provide it several poses and have it produce poses where I then drag the created pose onto the keyframe I want, and then make adjustments and handle the in betweens. Frankly AI is pretty good at posing something exactly as you want it, but it's reallyyy not that great at interpreting the inbetween. Other tooling I've set up is more based around IK. And I've also set up methods to easily import animations onto my skeleton from mocap or CC0  to act as bases. Also tools to facilitate layered animation/blending and hot swap between them, easily assign each to actions or conditions, etc.

AI can absolutely help simplify and streamline the otherwise very complicated workflows associated with animations.. but if you want AAA stuff it needs a lot of help. I have seen some very good animations made with AI, but the iterations it took were just not worth it. Your best bet of getting a good base are tools like motion capture or maybe trying to get AI to pose out a few frames based on some refs and use them as end effector constraints for nVidia's Kimodo.
